title: Same Text, Different Filename: Are LLM Judges Biased?
abstract: arXiv:2611.01829v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Yes. In 2026, leading economic journals started using Refine.ink in the technical quality assessment of submissions before publication. I study whether renaming a file changes the perception of the document's quality by LLM judges. I find that three frontier LLMs score the same document differently if you change the document's filename. A person-related label scores higher than no label; there is no consistent preference of own- or rival-based label, nor a penalty for an Asian name, but there is a context-specific bias in assessments whose direction and size vary with both document and label. With LLM-written documents, some self-premium can be detected, but a significant context-dependent label bias remains. Whether to combat it is a question of the costs of evaluation errors.

translated_title: 相同文本，不同文件名：大语言模型评审是否存在偏见？
translated_abstract: 是的。2026年，顶尖经济学期刊开始在发表前使用Refine.ink对投稿进行技术质量评估。我研究了重命名文件是否会改变大语言模型评审对文档质量的感知。我发现，如果更改文档的文件名，三个前沿大语言模型对同一文档的评分会有所不同。与人名相关的标签评分高于无标签的情况；对自己名字或对手名字的标签没有一致的偏好，对亚洲名字也没有惩罚，但评估中存在特定情境的偏见，其方向和大小随文档和标签的不同而变化。对于大语言模型撰写的文档，可以检测到一些自我溢价，但显著的情境依赖的标签偏见仍然存在。是否要对抗这种偏见是一个关于评估错误成本的问题。
tldr: 本研究通过实验发现三个前沿大语言模型对同一文档的评分会因文件名不同而变化，且这种标签偏见具有情境依赖性，其方向和大小随文档和标签的变化而变化。
en_tdlr: This study finds that three frontier LLM judges score the same document differently when the filename changes, revealing context-dependent label biases whose direction and magnitude vary with both the document and the label.
